text: What in your relationship right now would you not change?
evaluation: Open with affirmation before scrutiny. The 'not change' framing protects against the human reflex to start with complaint.

text: What in your relationship right now would you change if you could, with no consequence?
evaluation: The 'no consequence' clause is essential. It lets the unsayable surface without commitment.

text: When did you last feel chosen by your partner?
evaluation: If you reach for a recent moment, the relationship is alive. If you reach into the past, it is drifting.

text: When did you last feel unseen by your partner?
evaluation: Pair with rd003. The danger is the answer you do not say because you assume it isn't wanted.

text: What has your partner done lately that surprised you, in either direction?
evaluation: Surprise is the opposite of takenness-for-granted. Both directions are useful.

text: What did a partner once do that you have never told them bothered you?
evaluation: The point is the existence of the unsaid, not the litigation of the event.

text: What did a partner once do, without realising it, that meant a great deal to you?
evaluation: Counterpart to rd006. Always sit with both. The healthiest relationships have a longer list of these than of grievances.

text: What is the most generous interpretation of something a partner does that bothers you?
evaluation: Trains the muscle of charity. The ability to find one is itself the answer.

text: What do you wish a partner asked you about more often?
evaluation: Make a note of the answer. The question deserves to be asked unprompted.

text: What do you wish a partner asked you about less often?
evaluation: Care can become surveillance. Naming it gives both sides permission to recalibrate.

text: Where in your routine has love been hiding lately?
evaluation: Ordinary moments often carry more love than the marked occasions.

text: Where in your routine has resentment been hiding lately?
evaluation: Routines that look fair on paper can hide imbalance. Specificity is what pays.

text: What is the smallest thing you wish a partner would do, that they currently aren't?
evaluation: Bigness is not the bar. The smallness is the point.

text: What does a partner sometimes do that makes you feel like a child again, in the bad way?
evaluation: Names the regression triggers without forcing interpretation. Listen for somatic language.

text: What does a partner sometimes do that makes you feel like a child again, in the good way?
evaluation: The other side of the somatic frame. Often tiny and easy to repeat once named.

text: What version of yourself do you suspect a partner first fell for, that you still are?
evaluation: Healthy answers don't require perfect preservation — just a thread of continuity.

text: What version of yourself do you suspect a partner first fell for, that you are no longer — and is that loss or growth?
evaluation: The 'or' is the work. Make the choice gently, then explore the answer.

text: What part of you do you suspect a partner sees better than anyone else?
evaluation: An esteem question. Whether you can let yourself believe it is part of the answer.

text: What part of you do you suspect a partner has begun to miss?
evaluation: Hard to face. Easier after rd018.

text: What is one thing you have been carrying alone in this relationship that you don't have to?
evaluation: The first answer is rarely the real one. Wait.

text: What in your intimate life is good, and is there a version that would be better?
evaluation: The 'good first' frame matters. Honesty about wishes flows more easily after affirmation.

text: What in your intimate life is hard to say out loud, and what would help you say it?
evaluation: The second clause is the gift. Don't promise the help; ask for the conditions.

text: When do you feel most desired by a partner?
evaluation: Often answered with non-sexual moments. That is information.

text: When do you feel least desired by a partner?
evaluation: Pair with rd023. Listen for whether the answer is 'never' (avoidance) or specific (truth).

text: What are you afraid to admit you want from a partner?
evaluation: What stays unsaid because it feels too much to ask is usually exactly worth asking.

text: What are you afraid to admit you don't want from a partner?
evaluation: Sometimes the unspoken is what you would happily stop doing if granted permission.

text: What is one shared decision you and a partner have been postponing without naming it?
evaluation: Children, moves, money, the dog. Postponed decisions accumulate weight quietly.

text: What is one shared decision you privately regret?
evaluation: Adult question. Sit with it without re-litigating.

text: What did the last hard year teach you about your partner?
evaluation: Cross-checking the lessons reveals where you were actually present.

text: What did the last hard year teach you about yourself, that a partner helped reveal?
evaluation: Credit-giving is not flattery. It is an audit of mutual influence.

text: What in your day, lately, does a partner not know about?
evaluation: Long relationships drift into shorthand. The texture lost there matters more than people think.

text: What in your inner life, lately, does a partner not know about?
evaluation: Distinct from rd031. Some couples share days but not interiors.

text: What is one place you would like to go with a partner that you have not asked for?
evaluation: Wishes left unspoken often grow into resentments. Say the wish out loud.

text: What is one habit you and a partner share that no longer fits the people you have become?
evaluation: Couples accumulate habits that worked once. Naming the obsolete is the first step to changing it.

text: What is one fear about your relationship that you have been keeping small to be kind?
evaluation: Acknowledges that withholding is sometimes generosity. Permission to say it changes its weight.

text: What do you trust a partner with that you do not trust anyone else with?
evaluation: Names what has been earned. Worth saying back to each other in plain terms.

text: What do you not trust a partner with, and is that yours to fix or theirs?
evaluation: The second clause separates accountability from blame. Both can be true.

text: What is one thing a partner does that other people quietly find difficult, and that you have shielded them from hearing?
evaluation: Partners often filter outside feedback. The filter is its own form of love and its own risk.

text: What is the kindest thing a partner has done for you that you never said you noticed?
evaluation: Lighter, restorative — use after a heavier stretch.

text: What is the kindest thing you have done for a partner that they didn't notice?
evaluation: Sit with the asymmetry without resentment. Just acknowledge it.

text: What in your relationship's friendship has grown larger than its romance, and is that strength or quiet problem?
evaluation: Long-term couples often shift toward kinship. The question forces an honest read.

text: What in your relationship's romance is bigger than its friendship, and is that sustainable?
evaluation: The reverse imbalance. Both are common. Neither is stable forever.

text: What is one thing you used to do together that you would love to bring back?
evaluation: Light, concrete, often acted on within the week.

text: What is one thing you used to do together that you are right not to do anymore?
evaluation: Affirms growth without nostalgia. Useful counterbalance to rd043.

text: What does loyalty mean to you, and where would you say its limit lies?
evaluation: Better to know the limits in calm than to discover them in crisis.

text: What does fidelity mean to you, beyond the obvious?
evaluation: Definitions diverge more than couples assume. Better to discover the gap on a calm Sunday than later.

text: What would you need from a partner to feel you could be old together?
evaluation: Reframes the long horizon as something earned daily, not assumed.

text: What would you need from yourself to feel you could be old with someone?
evaluation: The mirror. Equally important.

text: What part of yourself do you still hide from a partner?
evaluation: Some hiding is healthy. Some isn't. The question is which kind yours is.

text: What part of you do you suspect a partner has noticed you hide, even if neither of you names it?
evaluation: Their guess, if you let yourself imagine it, is often surprisingly accurate.

text: What is something a partner does that you find easier to live with than to talk about?
evaluation: Names the small accommodations that build into resentment over years.

text: What do you do for a partner that you would quietly stop, if you could without consequence?
evaluation: A test of your tolerance for honesty with yourself. Painful, useful, rarely as catastrophic as feared.

text: What is the unfinished conversation between you and a partner?
evaluation: There is always one. The naming is most of the work.

text: What conversation between you and a partner did you finish well, that you should remember you can?
evaluation: Recall is repair. The point is to remember you have the muscle.

text: What is one ritual in your relationship you should never let drop?
evaluation: Your answer is the budget. Build the rest around it.

text: What is one ritual in your relationship you could let drop without losing anything?
evaluation: Frees up energy and trust both.

text: When you imagine the relationship in five years, what is unchanged?
evaluation: What you preserve in the imagination is what you value most now.

text: When you imagine the relationship in five years, what is different?
evaluation: Together with rd057, you get a sketch of your direction.

text: When you imagine the relationship in five years and feel afraid, what is the picture?
evaluation: Don't argue with the fear. Hear it, in detail. Then name what would prevent it.

text: What do you wish friends understood about your relationship?
evaluation: Reveals what gets misread from outside. Often clarifies how the couple narrates itself.

text: What do you wish a partner's family understood about your relationship?
evaluation: Names the in-law tension without forcing a fight.

text: What is one boundary with your own family that you have not held, but could?
evaluation: An accountability question. Sit with it before reacting.

text: What is one boundary with your partner's family you have appreciated, quietly?
evaluation: Counterweight to rd062. Both deserve airtime.

text: What do you do, when something between you and a partner is hard, that helps?
evaluation: Self-knowledge of repair behaviour. Worth naming so you can ask for it explicitly later.

text: What does a partner do, when something between you is hard, that helps?
evaluation: Pair with rd064. Naming what works keeps it from being accidental.

text: What do you do, when something between you and a partner is hard, that doesn't help — even though you think it does?
evaluation: The most useful answer in this whole bank, if you can sit with it without defending.

text: What is one apology you owe a partner that you have not given?
evaluation: Don't write the answer unless you intend to give it.

text: What is one apology you are owed by a partner that has not been given?
evaluation: The right answer is sometimes 'none'. Listen for whether yours is reflex or considered.

text: What is one thing a partner has forgiven you for that you have not forgiven yourself for?
evaluation: Sometimes the work after a couple's repair is internal.

text: What is one thing you have forgiven a partner for that you have not fully let go of?
evaluation: A second-order question. Useful before it bursts unexpectedly later.

text: What do you most want to say to a partner today that you have not?
evaluation: Receive whatever lands without re-routing.

text: What do you most want to ask a partner today that you have not?
evaluation: Hand yourself the keys to the conversation.

text: What of yours does a partner carry without complaint, that you should know about?
evaluation: Even small things compound when invisible. Naming them is most of their relief.

text: What of a partner's do you carry without complaint, that they only suspect?
evaluation: Naming the silent labour matters even when undramatic.

text: What did you assume about a new partner that turned out to be wrong?
evaluation: A safe-feeling question that often surfaces real updates about how you read people early on.

text: What did you sense early in a relationship that the other person took longer to see in themselves?
evaluation: An esteem-and-credit question. Most people can answer faster than they expect.

text: What did the early version of your relationship know that the current version has forgotten?
evaluation: Often surfaces something concrete and easy to bring back.

text: What does the current version of your relationship know that the early version couldn't?
evaluation: Affirms the present without dismissing the past.

text: What is one weakness of yours that a partner has made room for, that you would like to need less room for?
evaluation: An accountability question for yourself. Sit with it gently.

text: What is one strength of yours that has made room for a partner to rest?
evaluation: Restores balance after rd079. Use as a pair.

text: What money decision in your relationship has never really been discussed, only tolerated?
evaluation: Money is the under-discussed engine. Specificity is the win.

text: What money decision in your relationship have you made well together that you have never said out loud?
evaluation: Money harmony rarely gets celebrated. Try to.

text: What is one thing about your work life you wish a partner would ask you about?
evaluation: Long couples narrow their interest in each other's work; the cost is invisible until it is not.

text: What is one thing about your work life you would rather a partner stop asking about?
evaluation: Counterpart. Some work questions become surveillance over time.

text: What is one need of yours that has changed that a partner has not yet caught up to?
evaluation: Partners stop refreshing the model. Refresh it on purpose.

text: What is one need of a partner's that has changed that you have quietly accommodated?
evaluation: Naming silent kindnesses keeps them from going cold.

text: What part of parenting (or not parenting) feels different than you expected?
evaluation: Open in either direction. Childless answers are just as honest.

text: What part of being a partner feels different than you expected?
evaluation: Let the surprises sit. They map the gap between fantasy and practice.

text: What is one thing you have quietly let go of in your relationship that you suspect a partner could also release?
evaluation: Invitational, not coercive.

text: What is one thing you have not let go of, that you don't want to?
evaluation: Some things should not be released. Knowing which is part of love.

text: What in your days do you secretly love that you would never put on a list?
evaluation: The trivial-feeling answer is usually the truest.

text: What in your nights do you secretly love that you would never put on a list?
evaluation: Pair with rd091. Days and nights have different textures.

text: What is the smallest beauty in your home?
evaluation: A noticing question. Reorients attention.

text: What is the smallest annoyance in your home that you have stopped seeing?
evaluation: Often funny. Often easy to fix.

text: What in a partner would you defend to a stranger first?
evaluation: An esteem question disguised as a hypothetical.

text: What in a partner would you not defend to a stranger — and what would you say instead?
evaluation: A more searching variant. Listen for honest distinctions.

text: What in this reflection have you almost said to yourself and then not?
evaluation: Late-session catch. Often the truest line of the night is in there.

text: What in this reflection has surprised you, in either direction?
evaluation: Closing softening. Names what landed.

text: What is one practice you would like to adopt before you sit with these questions again?
evaluation: Turns the session into a habit. Specific, small, repeatable.

text: What do you want for yourself, just for tonight, that has nothing to do with anything you have just reflected on?
evaluation: Closer. Often the answer is small and specific. Honour it.
